newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to higher Thursday despite rising spot power supply and generally mild weather in the western U.S.

In over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $26.00-27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's settlement of 26.49, and July California-Oregon Border (COB) at $17.00-17.25 against yesterday's $16.69 close.
Yesterday, an attempt to rally the complex fizzled with August prices hit especially hard in a late sell-off.
Without fresh fundamental news, the front month contracts will likely test limits of their recent trading ranges, market sources said.
Analysts pegged support for July COB support in the $16.00 area and resistance near $17.50, while support for July PV in the $25.00 area and resistance in the $28.00-29.00 range.

A 450 megawatt (MW) unit at the San Juan coal-fired plant in New Mexico is expected to restart Thursday, and a 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired station in Washington is scheduled to return to service this weekend.
Forecasters called temperatures in the Northwest to run near to above normal next week with bouts of unsettled weather conditions.
Fair and warm weather is expected to stay in the Southwest with readings averaging three to six degrees F above normal through middle of next week.

Separately, industry sources told Reuters Wednesday that a a Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is proposing a summertime rating for the Pacific Intertie of 6,900 MW down from the current springtime limit of 7,200 MW.
